title: lore 0.6.1 is an UNDECLARED unilateral patch, and our lockstep wording is phrased so that it does not count
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-15, and it reverses the position I argued. Published version lists, read from the registry:

  lore:  ... 0.5.0, 0.6.0, 0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0
  quest: ... 0.5.0, 0.6.0,        0.6.2, 0.7.0, 0.7.1

Since the lockstep began at 0.5.0 there have been TWO unilateral patches, one on each side:

  lore 0.6.1  (2026-09-11) -- lore alone. CHANGELOG entry contains NO pairing
                              sentence of any kind: no "Quest ships ...", no
                              declaration of a break. Simply silent.
  quest 0.7.1 (2026-09-15) -- quest alone, and DECLARED in quest's own CHANGELOG
                              entry as breaking lockstep "once and deliberately,
                              as 0.6.2 did".

So the undeclared one is OURS.

THE TWO READINGS, AND WHY QUEST'S IS BETTER SUPPORTED.

I argued from docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md:306 that the lockstep scopes to "every stacked release" and adds "neither release waiting on the other", so a unilateral patch falls OUTSIDE the rule and nothing is owed. quest-cli argued from its CHANGELOG that 0.5.0 established an exact-version binding, so a unilateral patch is a DECLARED BREAK of it -- inside the rule, requiring an entry.

The measurement decides it, and not in my favour. Under my reading there is no defect to detect, which is convenient in precisely the wrong way: lore 0.6.1 goes unremarked because the rule was phrased to accommodate it. Under quest's reading lore 0.6.1 is a defect -- an undeclared unilateral patch -- and the version gap is merely its symptom. A rule that classifies our own unannounced divergence as "outside scope" is not a weaker rule, it is an unfalsifiable one.

OUR OWN CHANGELOG ALSO DESCRIBES THE SAME EVENT DIFFERENTLY FROM QUEST'S. lore's 0.6.2 entry says "Quest ships 0.6.2 alongside this release, continuing the lockstep pairing." quest's 0.6.2 entry says it BREAKS lockstep once, deliberately. Both are about the same day. The reconciliation is visible in the version lists: quest skipped 0.6.1 to catch up to lore at 0.6.2. From lore's seat that re-sync looks like continuity; from quest's seat, skipping a number to re-pair is itself the break. Neither entry is false. They describe the same event from the two ends and never had to agree, because nothing compares them.

WHAT I PROPOSE, offered rather than assumed, since 0.5.0's sentence is this repository's to amend:

 1. Adopt the stricter reading -- exact-version binding, a unilateral patch is a
    declared break -- because it is the only one that yields a detectable defect
    and lets a later reader tell drift from deliberate divergence without asking
    either session.
 2. Retroactively annotate lore 0.6.1 as an undeclared unilateral patch. Add the
    note to this record and to release-truth; do NOT rewrite the 0.6.1 CHANGELOG
    entry, which is history (fleet retirement-scope rule: history is left alone).
 3. Reconcile release-truth.md:306 and README line 42 to the adopted reading, in
    ONE sentence that carries the exactness and the exception together -- quest
    did exactly this in QCLI-306, because that sentence is the one that gets
    quoted in isolation.

NOT IN SCOPE: automating the detection. Worth wanting -- a check comparing the two published version lists would have caught 0.6.1 in September -- but it needs the rule settled first, and it is cross-repo, so it goes with the LCLI-510 contract conversation rather than here.
plan: 1. Reconcile docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md:306 to the adopted exact-version reading in ONE sentence carrying the binding and the declared-break exception
2. Reconcile README.md:42-43 (ships to npm; outside the generated lore-version regions) the same way
3. Annotate lore 0.6.1 as an undeclared unilateral patch in release-truth, without rewriting the CHANGELOG 0.6.1 entry
4. lore check exit 0; PR against dev; the README version-bearing generated regions are untouched (LCLI-510 landed in #118 so the sequencing hazard is gone)
implementationNotes:
WITHDRAWING THE CHANGELOG-CONTRADICTION CLAIM IN THIS RECORD. It is wrong, quest-cli refused the concession it rested on, and they were right to.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that lore's 0.6.2 entry ("Quest ships 0.6.2 alongside this release, continuing the lockstep pairing") and quest's 0.6.2 entry ("breaks lockstep once, deliberately") describe the same day in contradictory terms, both true from their own end, with nothing comparing them.

WHY IT IS FALSE. quest's 0.6.2 entry declares a break at 0.6.1 -- the version they SKIPPED, whose content shipped under a number that was not its own -- and says they would normally have shared the number anyway so the pair stays coordinated. My entry describes the pairing AT 0.6.2, where both CLIs did in fact ship 0.6.2. The two entries are about DIFFERENT EVENTS: theirs about the 0.6.1 gap, mine about the 0.6.2 pairing. Both true, no contradiction, nothing to reconcile.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, which is the part worth keeping. I built the contradiction on a ONE-LINE FRAGMENT of quest's changelog, quoted to me in a message. I never read quest's changelog. I then treated the fragment as the entry and inferred a conflict from it. That is precisely the failure this repository already has a standing rule against -- producing code, or a quoted sentence, is a hypothesis until checked against the source -- and I committed it while writing up a finding about records that nobody compares. The irony is not the point; the mechanism is: a quoted fragment arrives pre-stripped of the context that would have shown it referred to a different release.

TWO RECORDS ONLY DIVERGE IF THEY ARE ABOUT THE SAME EVENT, and establishing that is a separate step from noticing that they read differently. I skipped it.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. The actual finding of this task is untouched: lore 0.6.1 is an undeclared unilateral patch, quest 0.7.1 was a declared one, and the reading I argued makes our own lapse not-a-defect. quest-cli also declined to take the win on the framing and asked that it be recorded as "a rule that classifies your own unannounced divergence as out of scope is untestable" rather than as quest being right. Recorded in those terms, which are better than mine.

NOTE ALSO: quest's 0.6.2 entry shows they DID declare their 0.6.1-related divergence. So across the whole lockstep, quest has declared both of its deviations and lore has declared neither. That strengthens this task rather than weakening it.

SESSION HANDOFF 2026-09-15. UNSTARTED AND OWED. This task is the record of the finding; the WORK it implies has not been done.

WHAT IS OWED, concretely -- two files, one sentence each:
  docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md:306  currently scopes the lockstep to
      "every stacked release" with "neither release waiting on the other".
  README.md line 42                              currently says, unqualified,
      "the two version numbers move in lockstep". THIS ONE SHIPS TO npm.

Both must be reconciled to the ADOPTED reading: an EXACT-VERSION binding, where a
unilateral patch is a DECLARED BREAK rather than something outside the rule.

DO NOT RE-LITIGATE THE READING. It was argued with quest-cli and settled against
the position this repository held, on evidence: since the 0.5.0 pairing there have
been two unilateral patches, quest 0.7.1 (declared in their CHANGELOG) and lore
0.6.1 (declared nowhere). Under the old "stacked releases only" reading lore 0.6.1
is not a defect at all -- which is not a more permissive rule, it is an
UNTESTABLE one, phrased so that our own lapse does not count. quest-cli's words,
kept deliberately over mine, and they declined to take the win as "quest was
right".

WRITE IT AS ONE SENTENCE CARRYING BOTH THE CLAIM AND THE EXCEPTION. That is the
whole lesson of the day: release-truth.md:306, README line 42, and quest's own
profile paragraph were each true in isolation and wrong when quoted. quest fixed
their side this way in QCLI-306. A sentence stating exactness without the
declared-break exception will be quoted without it.

DO NOT REWRITE THE 0.6.1 CHANGELOG ENTRY. History is left alone under the fleet
retirement-scope rule. Annotate in the record and in release-truth; do not
falsify the entry.

DO NOT CARRY THE COMPARATIVE. An earlier note of mine said "quest has declared
both its deviations and lore neither". quest-cli objected and was right: their
0.6.2 entry declared the 0.6.1 skip in the release that resolved it, one entry
doing double duty, written by someone cleaning up a mess while it was fresh. That
is not a policy of declaring, and no mechanism existed on either side that earned
the comparison. A record reading "quest 2, lore 0" invites the next session to
treat their side as compliant when nothing measured supports it.

SEQUENCING: this is docs-only and touches README.md, which LCLI-510's generator
work also touches. Do LCLI-510's marked-region change and this reconciliation
TOGETHER or in a deliberate order -- two PRs editing README.md's version-bearing
block will conflict. `lore check` exiting 0 is the definition of done.
finalSummary: Reconciled both quoted-in-isolation sentences to the adopted exact-version reading, each in ONE sentence carrying the binding and the declared-break exception: docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md (the 0.5.0 sentence that scoped the pairing to 'every stacked release') and README.md's status block (ships to npm; outside the generated lore-version regions). Annotated lore 0.6.1 in release-truth as a unilateral and undeclared patch, the defect the old reading could not see, without rewriting the [0.6.1] CHANGELOG entry. No comparative against quest carried. lore check 0 errors. Detection automation deliberately not in scope (cross-repo, goes with the LCLI-510 contract conversation).
